name: Baybars Destroys Antioch, End of the Crusader Principality
summary: Mamluk Sultan Baybars captures and systematically destroys Antioch in May 1268, killing or enslaving the entire population. Prince Bohemond VI is absent in Tripoli; Baybars writes him a letter sarcastically describing the destruction. Antioch, one of the original Crusader principalities, is completely eliminated; the city never recovers its former importance.

_quarry.structural_significance: Baybars's campaign demonstrates the Mamluk strategy of systematic elimination rather than gradual pressure; Antioch's destruction removes the northernmost Crusader state and exposes Tripoli; Baybars's military genius (also defeating the Mongols at Ain Jalut, 1260) makes him the most formidable opponent the Crusader states face; his letter to Bohemond is a masterpiece of psychological warfare, rubbing in the extent of the destruction in formal diplomatic language
